paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Appeal No.176 of 2005
Kala S/o Sakru
R/o village Gadarjudda,
P.S. Manglor, District Haridwar. .......Appellant
 (On bail)
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand. .......Respondent
Mrs. Pushpa Joshi, Senior Advocate with Mr. D.C. Joshi and Mr. Saurabh
Adhikari, Advocates for the appellant.
Mrs. Mamta Bisht, learned A.G.A. with Ms. Sangeeta Miyan, learned Brief Holder
for the State.
Dated: March 21, 2013
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J. (Oral)
 Heard Mrs. Pushpa Joshi, Senior
Advocate with Mr. Deep Chandra Joshi and Mr.
Saurabh Adhikari, Advocates for the accused/
appellant and Mrs. Mamta Bisht, A.G.A. with Ms.
Sangita Miyan, Brief Holder for the State.
2. After the order for issuance of bailable
warrant against the appellant was passed, instant
warrant recall application is moved for recalling the
order. The application is duly supported by an
affidavit.
3. Considering the submission of learned
counsel for the accused/appellant, order passed
today for issuance of bailable warrant against the
appellant is hereby recalled. CRMA No. 377 of 2013
stands disposed of.
4. Heard learned counsel for the parties on
merits also.

2
5. This appeal, preferred under Section 374
(2) of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short
Cr.P.C.), is directed against the judgment and order
dated 26.09.2005, passed by the District and
Sessions Judge, Haridwar, in Sessions Trial No. 165
of 2003, whereby the said court has convicted
accused/appellant Kala under Section 376, 506
I.P.C. and sentenced him under Section 376 I.P.C.
to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of
seven years and directed to pay fine of ` 2,000/-, in
default of payment of fine a further imprisonment of
two months under Section 376 I.P.C. and six
months rigorous imprisonment under Section 506
I.P.C.
6. In nut-shell, the prosecution case is that
on 02.04.2003 at 7:00 p.m., P.W.1 Babu Ram
(husband of the victim) lodged F.I.R. (Ext. A-1) at
Police Station Manglor, District Haridwar with the
averment that on previous night i.e. on 01.04.2003
he had gone to Delhi for some urgent piece of work,
leaving alone at home his wife and children. On
02.04.2003 at 8:00 a.m., his wife Smt. Baby had
gone to jungle to ease herself, where the appellant-Kala S/o Sakru caught hold of his wife and
committed rape upon her. The accused threatened
his wife that if she will disclose the incident to
anyone, he will kill her. It was further asserted in
the F.I.R. that when the complainant came back
from Delhi, his wife narrated him the entire
incident. On the basis of said report, Chik report
(Ex. A-9) was prepared and a crime no. 80 of 2003

3
was registered in respect of offences punishable
under Sections 376 and 506 of I.P.C., against the
accused Kala. Investigation was taken up by PW-5
Sub Inspector S.P. Bishnoi, who interrogated the
witnesses and started investigation. The
Investigating Officer, after conducting spot
inspection, prepared site-plan (Ext. A-4). The
trouser (SALWAR) of the victim and underwear of
the accused were taken in possession and memos
(Ext. A-5 and Ext. A-6) were prepared. The victim
Smt. Baby was medically examined by PW-4 Dr.
Neelam Kandari on 02.04.2003 at J.N.S.M. Govt.
Hospital, Roorkee, who prepared medical
examination report Ext. A-2 and on the basis of the
report of the Radiologist, she prepared
supplementary medical report (Ext.A-3). The trouser
of the victim and underwear of the accused were
sent for chemical examination and report of the
FSL, Agra was received which is Ext.A-8 on record.
After completion of investigation, the Investigating
Officer submitted charge sheet (Ext. A-7) against the
accused Kala, for his trial in respect of offences
punishable under Sections 376 and 506 of I.P.C.
7. The Chief Judicial Magistrate, Haridwar,
on receipt of the charge sheet, after giving necessary
copies to the accused, as required under section
207 Cr.P.C., committed the case to the Court of
Sessions for trial on 18.06.2003. After hearing the
parties on 14.07.2003, learned Sessions Judge,
Haridwar, framed charge of offences punishable
under section 376 and 506 of I.P.C, to which the

4
accused Kala pleaded not guilty and claimed to be
tried. On this, prosecution got examined PW-1 Babu
Ram, complainant, PW-2 Smt. Baby, victim, PW-Chottey Ram, PW-4 Dr. Neelam Kandari and PW-5
Sub Inspection S.P. Bishnoi, Investigation Officer.
Oral and documentary evidence was put to the
accused under section 313 Cr.P.C., in reply to
which he alleged that the evidence adduced against
him is false. The accused produced DW-1 Smt.
Angoori in his defence. After hearing the parties, the
trial Court found accused, Kala, guilty of charge of
offences punishable under Section 376 and 506 of
I.P.C., and convicted him accordingly. Aggrieved by
judgment and order dated 26.09.2005, passed by
Sessions Judge, Haridwar, in Sessions Trial No. 165
of 2003, instant appeal has been preferred by the
convict.
8. Before further discussion, this Court
thinks it just and proper to mention the
observations made by PW-4 Dr. Neelam Kandari,
after medical examination of Smt. Baby, victim, on
02.04.2003. The observations made by the Medical
Officer in the medical report of the victim (Ext. A-2)
are being reproduced below:
"Hymen is torn, old healed tears
present. She is multipara. No
evidence of injury on internal parts.
She is used to sexual intercourse
previously. No evidence of struggle
found on body. For age, case was
referred to Radiologist. For evidence
of rape, slide of vaginal smear sent
for examination. "

5
9. A supplementary Medical Report was also
filed by Dr. Neelam Kandari based on the report of
Radiologist. The victim was found more than 18
years. No definite opinion was given about rape. She
was found multiparous woman. No sign of struggle
was found. No sign of spermatozoa dead or alive
was found in pathology test.
10. PW-1 Babu Ram is the complainant, who
has stated that the incident was of 02.04.2003. He
had gone to Delhi on 01.04.2003. His wife and five
children were at home. On the date of incident at
8:00 a.m. his wife Smt. Baby had gone out to ease
herself. At that moment, the accused Kala came
there and after catching hold of his wife in a
sugarcane field, the accused threatened her to kill
and committed rape upon her. Thereafter, the
accused fled from the scene. While coming out from
sugarcane field in running position, the accused
was seen by Chottey Ram PW-3. He further stated
that when he returned from Delhi on 02.04.2003
and reached his home at 6:00 p.m. then his wife
narrated the entire incident to him. He scribed the
written report from his brother Sateshwar, who after
scribing the report read it over to him and thereafter
signed it. He proved the written report Ext. A-1. On
03.04.2003, he handed over the trouser of his wife
to the Investigating Officer, which was kept in a
sealed cover.
11. PW-2 is Smt. Baby, the victim, who has
stated that the incident was of 11⁄4 years' back. Her
husband had gone to Delhi. On that day at 8:00

6
a.m., she had gone out in a sugarcane field to ease
herself and just after she sat to ease her, the
accused Kala appeared, who forcefully caught hold
of her and committed rape on her. She tried to
make shrieks, but the accused threatened to kill her
and after committing rape on her, the accused fled.
Her younger brother-in-law had seen the accused in
running position from sugarcane field. She
narrated the entire incident to her husband, when
he returned from Delhi.
12. PW-3 is the witness Chottey Ram, who
has stated that on 02.04.2003 at 8:00-8:15 a.m., he
was going towards the fields and when he reached
to the field of Dharmveer, he saw the accused Kala
in running state, thereafter he had seen wife of
Babu Ram, namely, Baby coming from the field. He
identified the accused Kala, who was present in the
Court.
13. PW-4 is Dr. Neelam Kandari, Medical
Officer, who conducted the medical examination of
the victim. Description of her statement has already
been mentioned in preceding paragraphs.
14. PW-5 Sub Inspector S.P. Bishnoi, is the
Investigating Officer, who proved the site-plan Ext.
A-4, memo of taking in possession the trouser of the
victim Ext. A-5 and memo in taking possession the
underwear of the accused Ext. A-6, Charge-sheet
Ext.A-7, the report of FSL Ext. A-8, Chik FIR Ext. A-9 and copy of G.D. Ext. A-10.

7
15. At the outset, the question before this
Court is as to whether at the time of incident, the
accused committed rape upon Smt. Baby forcefully
against her wishes and consent, and whether in
furtherance of his intention, the accused threatened
the victim to cause grievous hurt to her, as
suggested by the prosecution.
16. Mrs. Pushpa Joshi, learned Senior
Advocate for the accused/ appellant argued that as
per the evidence discussed above, the guilt of the
accused is not proved and the trial Court has
wrongly convicted the accused/ appellant for the
offence punishable under Sections 376 and 506
I.P.C. Submission of the learned Senior Advocate for
the appellant is that as per the evidence produced
by the prosecution, the prosecution has failed to
prove its case beyond reasonable doubt against the
accused. She contended that the conviction is
against the weight of evidence on record, illegal,
unwarranted and bad in the eyes of law, and that
the sentence is too severe. She contended that to
prove the guilt of rape, the medical report of the
victim should be creditable and potential. She
contended that in the case of forceful rape
committed against the wishes and consent of a
woman that too on a rough field like sugarcane,
there should have been signs of external injuries or
marks of struggle on any part of the body of the
victim. She submitted that the medical report of the
victim conducted by PW-4 Dr. Neelam Kandari,
clearly pointed out that no sign of external injury or

8
struggle were seen either on the private parts or on
the body of the victim at the time the victim was
medically examined. Further the doctor did not give
any opinion about the rape, as Smt. Baby was
found habitual to sexual intercourse previously.
Further, in the pathological test, the doctor did not
find any sign of spermatozoa, live or dead. She
contended that in such circumstances, the medical
report is in favour of the accused, which clearly
suggests that if rape was committed upon the victim
that was done with the consent of the victim.
Learned Senior Advocate for the appellant further
contended that the incident was of 02.04.2003 at
about 8:00 a.m. and the victim has disclosed the
incident to her husband only after he returned from
Delhi. Before it, she did not disclose the incident to
anyone nor her brother-in-law PW-3 Chottey Ram,
besides PW-3 Chottey Ram saw the accused, in
running position, at the site. What compelled the
victim to keep mum till the return of her husband?
Learned Senior Advocate for the appellant
contended, had the victim would have shrieked at
the time of catching hold of her by the accused, her
brother-in-law Chottey Ram PW-3 would have
rescued her. This conduct of the victim illustrated
that at the time of alleged incident of rape, the
victim did not make any hue and cry. She further
submitted that there is contradiction in the
statement of the victim, as at one point of time she
herself stated that she opened her trouser herself to
ease her but in her cross-examination, she alleged
that the accused forcefully removed her trouser. She

9
contended that though in the chemical analyses
sperms and spermatozoa were found in the trouser
of the victim and underwear of the accused, which
were found in category-A, however, it is not
established that sperm of category-A were
unquestionably of the accused, as no medical
examination of the accused was conducted by the
prosecution in order to match the sperm of
category-A found in the sealed material opened at
FSL.
17. Mrs. Mamta Bisht, learned A.G.A. for the
State submitted that the first information lodged in
this matter is prompt one. No enmity is established
in between the family of the victim and the accused.
Thus, the assumption to implicate the accused
falsely, leaving the actual culprit is nothing but a
concocted shelter? She submitted that considering
the fact that the rape was committed on the victim,
the sentence passed by the Court below is not too
severe.
18. I have considered the submissions
advanced by the learned counsel for the parties. I
am convinced with the argument advanced by
learned Senior Advocate for the appellant. It is
beyond imagination that besides the presence of
PW-3 Chottey Ram at the place of incident, the
victim did not complaint of the incident to him
rather she waited for the return of her husband.
What was the occasion to keep mum till the return
of her husband? Had the victim shrieked at the time
of catching hold of her by the accused, her brother-

10
in-law Chottey Ram PW-3 would have rescued her.
This conduct of the victim is overt which apparently
illustrates that at the time of alleged incident of
rape, the victim did not make any hue and cry for
her rescue. The victim is grown up lady. In the
event of forceful rape against her wish, she would
have resisted and struggled and by doing so, some
marks of struggle or external injuries were
inevitable. This was not found in medical
examination, which is the most salient and
noticeable factor. Absence of such mark of external
injuries on the person of the victim is fatal for the
prosecution to prove the guilt of the accused beyond
reasonable doubt. Even in pathology test, no
spermatozoa dead or alive were found.
19. For the reasons as discussed above, I am
of the view that it cannot be said that charge of
offence punishable under Sections 376 and 506
I.P.C. is proved beyond reasonable doubt against
the accused/ appellant Kala. In my opinion he is
entitled to the benefit of reasonable doubt.
Therefore, this appeal deserves to be allowed.
20. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
Impugned judgment and order dated 26.09.2005,
passed by Sessions Judge, Haridwar in Sessions
Trial No. 165 of 2003, so far as it relates to the
conviction and sentence awarded against the
accused/appellant Kala under Section 376 and 506
I.P.C., is hereby set-aside. He is on bail. He needs

11
not to surrender. His sureties are discharged. Let
the Lower Court's Record be sent back.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
 21.03.2013
